function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in the context of financial services (especially in wealth management, investment advisory, or banking) refers to a formal authorization that a client gives to a financial professional or institution to act on their behalf in managing their investments or financial affairs. Key points about a mandate: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Grants the advisor or institution the legal authority to make investment decisions, execute trades, manage portfolios, or handle other financial tasks for the client. | | **Types** | • **Active Mandate** – The advisor is actively managing the client’s portfolio.
• **Pending Mandate** – The mandate has been agreed upon but is awaiting activation (e.g., waiting for funds to be transferred).
• **Inactive Mandate** – The mandate has been terminated or paused. | | **Contents** | • Scope of authority (e.g., which asset classes can be traded).
• Investment objectives and risk tolerance.
• Fees and compensation structure.
• Duration and termination conditions. | | **Legal Basis** | Usually documented in a written agreement (often called a “Mandate Agreement” or “Investment Management Agreement”) that complies with regulatory requirements. | | **Why It Matters** | • Provides clarity on who can act and how.
• Helps regulators track who is managing client assets.
• Enables partners (e.g., banks, fintech platforms) to retrieve and monitor mandates for compliance and reporting. | In practice, when a client signs a mandate, the partner’s system will record it as an “active” mandate. If the client later wants to stop the service, the mandate becomes “inactive.” Pending mandates are those that have been signed but not yet fully operational (e.g., awaiting initial capital deposit).
